title: Splitting a finite sum
statement: For natural numbers $a,b$ and any function $f:\mathrm{Fin}(a+b)\to\mathbb{N}$, the sum of $f$ over the first $a+b$ indices equals the sum over the first $a$ indices plus the sum over the last $b$ indices: $\sum_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(a+b)} f(i)=\sum_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(a)} f(i+b)+\sum_{i\in\mathrm{Fin}(b)} f(a+i)$, where the terms are indexed by their corresponding positions in the full range.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps indices in $\mathrm{Fin}(a+b)$ to natural numbers
